text.p: The Maltese economy grew by four percent in real terms between January and September last year, compared with 6.3 percent in the same period of 1995, according to figures just issued by the Finance Ministry.
Nominal gross domestic product, at market prices, was estimated at 884.3 million pounds ($2.46 billion) compared to 827.5 million pounds in the first nine months of 1995.
The increase in GDP in 1996 was primarily due to an expansion in consumer and government spending.

Private consumption totalled 592.9 million pounds, up 12.3 percent in nominal terms or 9.3 percent in real terms, while government current expenditure rose 9.8 percent in nominal terms and 5.9 percent in real terms.

Finance Minister Lino Spiteri, presenting the 1997 Budget in the Maltese parliament on Monday, said that from the economic point of view, the drop in imports of industrial products and capital products was "a matter of concern", particularly as imports of consumer goods were up.
Malta recorded an inflation rate of 2.94 percent in the year to last September, down from the previous year, but higher than inflation in the island's main trading partners in Europe. ($=36 cents)
